title: The process atlas
subtitle: Trace reactions, host–pathogen processes, and drug journeys through interactive diagrams.

blocks.title: Trace a biochemical reaction
blocks.description: Authoring scaffold: replace the labels and mechanism details with your lecture content. The routes illustrate graph structure, not a clinical model.

nodes.title: Substrate
nodes.description: Define the starting molecule and its concentration or availability.

details.label: Input
details.value: Replace with the substrate name and relevant conditions.

nodes.title: Enzyme–substrate complex
nodes.description: Describe binding, cofactors, and the relevant catalytic mechanism.

details.label: Cofactor
details.value: Add a cofactor if this reaction requires one.

nodes.title: Product
nodes.description: Describe product formation and what controls reaction flux.

nodes.title: Competing pathway
nodes.description: Explain the competing route for the same substrate.

nodes.title: Regulator
nodes.description: Describe the regulator and the mechanism of inhibition for your chosen reaction.

blocks.title: Map pathogen development
blocks.description: Authoring scaffold: replace the labels and mechanism details with your lecture content. The routes illustrate graph structure, not a clinical model.

nodes.title: Exposure
nodes.description: Specify the pathogen, entry route, and relevant context.

nodes.title: Establishment
nodes.description: Explain how the selected pathogen establishes itself.

nodes.title: Host interaction
nodes.description: Explain the host–pathogen mechanisms relevant to this lecture.

nodes.title: Tissue injury
nodes.description: Connect the mechanisms to the observed tissue changes.

nodes.title: Clearance / resolution
nodes.description: Describe the conditions under which the process resolves.

nodes.title: Persistence
nodes.description: Explain the conditions supporting persistence in your chosen example.

blocks.title: Follow a drug journey
blocks.description: Authoring scaffold: replace the labels and mechanism details with your lecture content. The routes illustrate graph structure, not a clinical model.

nodes.title: Entry compartment
nodes.description: Specify the drug, formulation, route, and starting compartment. Adapt the topology to that route.

nodes.title: Central compartment
nodes.description: Describe how the drug enters and moves through the central compartment.

details.label: Exposure
details.value: Add relevant concentration and time information, with units and sources.

nodes.title: Target compartment
nodes.description: Explain distribution to the target and the relevant drug–target interaction.

details.label: Target
details.value: Specify the receptor, enzyme, or other target.

nodes.title: Response
nodes.description: Connect target interaction to the response discussed in the lecture.

nodes.title: Transformation
nodes.description: Specify the relevant transformation pathways and products for this drug.

nodes.title: Exit compartment
nodes.description: Describe the relevant elimination route and its constraints.
